field.label: Enable
field.help: Watch the selected interfaces and record per-device traffic.

field.label: Interfaces
field.help: The LAN or VLAN interfaces your devices are on. With a bridge, choose the bridge; WAN and a bridge's member ports aren't listed.

field.label: Local networks
field.help: Usually leave this empty: your devices' networks come from the interfaces' addresses. A transparent bridge has no address, so Loupe then treats private addresses as local. List networks here (e.g. 192.0.2.0/24) if devices use others, such as public addresses or IPv6.

field.label: Keep sites seen (days)
field.help: Site names each device used (from DNS answers and TLS and QUIC connections), kept to name its traffic and identify it.

field.label: Address
field.help: Loupe names devices as Home Assistant does and shows their area, for devices it knows by MAC address (most network integrations; cloud ones such as Tuya don't share it). Your own names in Loupe still win. Leave empty to not use it.

field.label: Access token
field.help: In Home Assistant: your profile (your name, bottom left) > Security > Long-lived access tokens > Create token. Name it Loupe and paste it here. Loupe only reads device names and areas.

field.label: Verify certificate
field.help: Turn off for a self-signed certificate (Home Assistant's default when it uses HTTPS without a domain).
